task.title: Age-bounded keyed batching
task.specification: Config limit>=1,delay>=1,required:boolean. Start time=0 and no pending keys. Events put{key,value}, cancel{key}, advance{dt>=0}, flush. Put stores/replaces the latest value for a key; replacement retains its first pending time. With required=true each put emits immediately and nothing is queued. Otherwise put flushes all pending keys when distinct-key count>=limit. Advance increases time and flushes all when any first pending age>=delay. Flush explicitly emits all; cancel silently removes only that key. Emission order is lexical key order. Output {emitted:[{key,value}],pending:[lexically sorted keys],now}. All emissions drain those keys. Values are safe integers. Implement pure solve({config,state,event})->{state,output}; initial state is null. Only the current event is available; each named event uses a type field, e.g. {type:"run"}. Inputs have at most eight single lowercase ASCII-letter identifiers, safe integer quantities and at most 48 events. Return exactly the documented output fields after every event; state representation is unrestricted JSON. All identifiers and numeric fields shown in event forms are present; quantities and all intermediate arithmetic are safe integers. Integral JSON number spellings such as 1 and 1.0 are equivalent; booleans remain distinct from numbers. Regimes vary event order and timing: ordinary uses moderate capacity, boundary tests equality/empty cases, adversarial repeats stale/conflicting events, and shift uses smaller capacities or larger costs/delays within the same semantics. Generator regimes: Boundary limit=2 versus ordinary 3; shift enables required delivery, disabling aggregation. Adversarial traces add adjacent repeated events, capped at 48; those events obey the same contract.

matchedCard.label: Paper chromatography
matchedCard.relation: Constituents carried through a stationary medium can move at different rates because their interactions with the moving and stationary phases differ. A combined mixture can therefore reveal separable components under a suitable choice of phases.
assumptions: The phases interact differently with the constituents of interest.
The observed migration conditions are comparable.
matchedCard.boundary: Similar migration does not by itself establish identity. Poorly distinguishing phases can leave constituents unresolved, and different phases can change their relative migration.
matchedCard.source_fact: The Royal Society of Chemistry describes chromatographic separation through different distributions or affinities between mobile and stationary phases.

shuffledCard.label: Astronomical adaptive optics
shuffledCard.relation: A reference measurement estimates a changing disturbance, and a corrector adjusts the observation path using that estimate. Correction remains useful only while the reference samples a relevant disturbance and the measurement-to-correction delay is sufficiently short.
assumptions: Reference and observed object experience sufficiently related disturbances.
The corrector can respond on the timescale of the disturbance.
shuffledCard.boundary: A stale or spatially unrepresentative reference can produce an inappropriate correction. Correcting the observation path does not establish the intrinsic state of the observed object.
shuffledCard.source_fact: ESO describes guide-star measurements controlling deformable mirrors in real time, with correction limited by temporal response and the atmospheric paths sampled by the reference.

initial.explanation: The rule is: pending values retain their first insertion time; replacements change only the value. A non-required batch drains when its distinct-key count reaches limit, when any key reaches delay age, or on flush, always in lexical order. Required puts bypass batching. For example, resetting age on replacement would incorrectly delay p1.
initial.mapping: config.limit and config.delay govern count and age triggers; config.required selects immediate delivery. State maps each pending key to {value,at}, plus now. Event effects produce emitted, pending, and now.
initial.assumptions: Inputs obey the stated legal-input constraints. Lexical order is JavaScript string ordering for single lowercase ASCII identifiers. Returned state is JSON data and is passed unchanged to the next call.
initial.holds: function holds(input,output){if(!applies(input)||!Array.isArray(output)||output.length!==input.events.length)return false;var c=input.config,n=0,p={},o=[];function keys(){return Object.keys(p).sort()}function drain(){var r=keys().map(function(k){return {key:k,value:p[k].v}});p={};return r}for(var e of input.events){var em=[];if(e.type==='put'){if(c.required)em=[{key:e.key,value:e.value}];else{if(!p[e.key])p[e.key]={v:e.value,t:n};else p[e.key].v=e.value;if(Object.keys(p).length>=c.limit)em=drain()}}else if(e.type==='cancel')delete p[e.key];else if(e.type==='advance'){n+=e.dt;if(Object.keys(p).some(function(k){return n-p[k].t>=c.delay}))em=drain()}else if(e.type==='flush')em=drain();var q=keys(),x=output[o.length];if(!x||x.now!==n||JSON.stringify(x.emitted)!==JSON.stringify(em)||JSON.stringify(x.pending)!==JSON.stringify(q))return false;o++}return true}
initial.program: function solve(x){var c=x.config,s=x.state||{now:0,pending:{}},e=x.event;var now=s.now,p=s.pending,em=[];function ks(){return Object.keys(p).sort()}function drain(){var a=ks();em=a.map(function(k){return {key:k,value:p[k].value}});p={}}if(e.type==='put'){if(c.required)em=[{key:e.key,value:e.value}];else{if(p[e.key]===undefined)p[e.key]={value:e.value,at:now};else p[e.key].value=e.value;if(Object.keys(p).length>=c.limit)drain()}}else if(e.type==='cancel'){delete p[e.key]}else if(e.type==='advance'){now+=e.dt;if(Object.keys(p).some(function(k){return now-p[k].at>=c.delay}))drain()}else if(e.type==='flush')drain();return {state:{now:now,pending:p},output:{emitted:em,pending:ks(),now:now}}}

final.explanation: Pending entries store their latest value and original insertion time. Non-required batches drain on reaching the distinct-key limit, when any pending entry reaches the delay, or on flush. Replacement updates only the value, while cancellation removes one key. Required puts emit immediately. Every emission and pending-key list is lexically sorted, and advance updates time before checking ages.
final.program: function solve(x){var c=x.config,s=x.state||{now:0,pending:{}},e=x.event,n=s.now,p=s.pending,em=[];function keys(){return Object.keys(p).sort()}function drain(){var a=keys();em=a.map(function(k){return {key:k,value:p[k].value}});p={}}if(e.type==='put'){if(c.required){em=[{key:e.key,value:e.value}]}else{if(p[e.key]===undefined)p[e.key]={value:e.value,at:n};else p[e.key].value=e.value;if(Object.keys(p).length>=c.limit)drain()}}else if(e.type==='cancel'){delete p[e.key]}else if(e.type==='advance'){n+=e.dt;if(Object.keys(p).some(function(k){return n-p[k].at>=c.delay}))drain()}else if(e.type==='flush')drain();return {state:{now:n,pending:p},output:{emitted:em,pending:keys(),now:n}}}

initial.explanation: Maintain current time and, for each pending key, its latest value and first pending time. Required puts emit immediately; otherwise capacity and age-triggered flushes drain all pending keys in lexical order.
initial.mapping: Keys map to pending records {value,at}; now is accumulated advance time; emitted is the drained lexical snapshot.
initial.assumptions: Event fields and config are valid as specified. Lexical order is JavaScript string order for lowercase ASCII keys.
initial.holds: function holds(input,output){if(!Array.isArray(output)||output.length!==input.events.length)return false;var c=input.config,s={now:0,k:{}};function keys(){return Object.keys(s.k).sort()}function flush(){var a=keys().map(function(x){return {key:x,value:s.k[x].v}});s.k={};return a}for(var i=0;i<input.events.length;i++){var e=input.events[i],a=[];if(e.type==='put'){if(c.required)a=[{key:e.key,value:e.value}];else{if(!s.k[e.key])s.k[e.key]={v:e.value,at:s.now};else s.k[e.key].v=e.value;if(Object.keys(s.k).length>=c.limit)a=flush()}}else if(e.type==='cancel')delete s.k[e.key];else if(e.type==='advance'){s.now+=e.dt;if(!c.required){var q=keys();for(var j=0;j<q.length;j++)if(s.now-s.k[q[j]].at>=c.delay){a=flush();break}}}else if(e.type==='flush')a=flush();var want={emitted:a,pending:keys(),now:s.now},got=output[i];if(JSON.stringify(got)!==JSON.stringify(want))return false}return true}

final.explanation: Tracks accumulated time and pending records containing each key’s latest value and original pending timestamp. Non-required puts trigger a lexical flush at capacity; advances flush when any pending record reaches the delay. Required puts emit immediately. Cancels remove only their key, and every emission drains all pending keys.

initial.explanation: Optional assistance: batching is useful only while pending entries remain temporally relevant; a deadline forces emission. This corresponds directly to the keyed batching contract, without changing any target requirement.
initial.mapping: Keys map to pending batches, first pending time maps to age, limit maps to capacity, and delay maps to deadline. Required mode bypasses batching.
initial.assumptions: Keys are lowercase ASCII identifiers and all supplied fields satisfy the stated validity constraints. Lexical order is ordinary JavaScript string order.
initial.holds: function holds(input,output){if(!applies(input)||!Array.isArray(output)||output.length!==input.events.length)return false;var c=input.config,n=0,m={},r=[];function keys(){return Object.keys(m).sort()}function emit(){var a=keys().map(function(k){return {key:k,value:m[k].v}});m={};return a}for(var e of input.events){var a=[];if(e.type==='put'){if(c.required){a=[{key:e.key,value:e.value}]}else{if(!(e.key in m))m[e.key]={v:e.value,t:n};else m[e.key].v=e.value;if(keys().length>=c.limit)a=emit()}}else if(e.type==='advance'){n+=e.dt;if(!c.required){var q=keys();for(var k of q)if(n-m[k].t>=c.delay){a=emit();break}}}else if(e.type==='cancel')delete m[e.key];else if(e.type==='flush')a=emit();var z={emitted:a,pending:keys(),now:n},o=output[r.length++];if(JSON.stringify(z)!==JSON.stringify(o))return false}return true}
initial.program: function solve(x){var c=x.config,e=x.event,s=x.state||{n:0,m:{}};var n=s.n,m=s.m,a=[];function ks(){return Object.keys(m).sort()}function flush(){var q=ks();a=q.map(function(k){return {key:k,value:m[k].v}});m={}}if(e.type==='put'){if(c.required)a=[{key:e.key,value:e.value}];else{if(m[e.key]===undefined)m[e.key]={v:e.value,t:n};else m[e.key].v=e.value;if(ks().length>=c.limit)flush()}}else if(e.type==='advance'){n+=e.dt;if(!c.required){var q=ks();for(var i=0;i<q.length;i++)if(n-m[q[i]].t>=c.delay){flush();break}}}else if(e.type==='cancel'){delete m[e.key]}else if(e.type==='flush')flush();return {state:{n:n,m:m},output:{emitted:a,pending:ks(),now:n}}}

final.explanation: Pending keys retain their first insertion time while values are replaced. Non-required puts flush at capacity; advances flush when any pending key reaches the delay, and explicit flushes/capacity flushes drain all keys in lexical order. Required mode emits puts immediately.
final.program: function solve(x){var c=x.config,e=x.event,s=x.state||{now:0,pending:{}};var now=s.now,p=s.pending,out=[];function keys(){return Object.keys(p).sort()}function flush(){var ks=keys();out=[];for(var i=0;i<ks.length;i++){var k=ks[i];out.push({key:k,value:p[k].value})}p={}}if(e.type==='put'){if(c.required){out=[{key:e.key,value:e.value}]}else{if(p[e.key]===undefined)p[e.key]={value:e.value,time:now};else p[e.key].value=e.value;if(keys().length>=c.limit)flush()}}else if(e.type==='cancel'){delete p[e.key]}else if(e.type==='advance'){now+=e.dt;if(!c.required){var ks=keys();for(var i=0;i<ks.length;i++){if(now-p[ks[i]].time>=c.delay){flush();break}}}}else if(e.type==='flush'){flush()}return{state:{now:now,pending:p},output:{emitted:out,pending:keys(),now:now}}}
